draft.title: Factors in sentencing
card: Aggravating factor
A feature of the offence or offender that can make the sentence more severe, such as a weapon being used or a prior record of similar offences.
Mitigating factor
A feature that can make the sentence less severe, such as genuine remorse, good prospects of rehabilitation or a difficult personal background.
Guilty plea
An early plea of guilty can lead to a lower sentence. It saves court time and spares witnesses and victims from giving evidence.
Victim impact statement
The victim can tell the court how the offence has affected them. The judge may consider it when weighing the harm done.
draft.remember: The judge weighs factors that can increase or reduce a sentence, along with a guilty plea and the victim's account of harm.

a.q: Which of these is a mitigating factor at sentencing?
opts: The offender shows genuine remorse
The offender has prior convictions for similar offences
The offender used a weapon in the offence
The offender planned the offence in advance
a.why: Genuine remorse can reduce a sentence, so it mitigates. The other three can make a sentence more severe, so they aggravate. Prior similar convictions are the most tempting wrong option, but they count against the offender.
a.clue: Which one could lead to a lighter sentence?

b.q: Sam pleaded guilty to a burglary in Bendigo at the first hearing. The homeowner's victim impact statement describes ongoing fear at home. How may the judge use these?
opts: Plea may reduce the sentence, statement shows the harm
Both are aggravating factors that raise the sentence
Statement is ignored, as only the plea can matter
The sentence is cut because the victim has suffered
b.why: An early guilty plea can reduce the sentence, and the victim impact statement helps the judge understand the harm done. The plea is not aggravating, and the victim's suffering is weighed as harm, not as a reason to reduce the sentence.
b.clue: One of these can lower the sentence and the other shows the harm.

b.best: Plea may reduce the sentence, statement shows the harm
